newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan brokers say surprised by deregulation plan.
newsitem.headline: Japan brokers say surprised by deregulation plan.

text.p: The chairman of the Japan Securities Dealers Association said on Thursday he was surprised with a bold deregulation proposal made by a subcommittee of an advisory council to the prime minister.

Masashi Suzuki said the proposal, calling for abolition of all finance market regulations in principle, sets a nearby time schedule for the deregulation, despite the fact each issue will have a great impact on the securities industry.
Suzuki said he expects the council to hold further discussions as the proposals would be used as an outline for the council's final recommendation.

The subcommittee presented its proposal to the panel earlier today, urging the abolition of all rules on the range of business which subsidiaries of banks and brokers are allowed to engage in and liberalisation of stockbroking fees. It said deregulation should be implemented by the end of March 2000.

Panel chairman Koichi Minaguchi told reporters that the ministries concerned all agree that they are heading in the direction outlined in the report, but when it comes to specifics, they said they still have different opinions.
The panel's final proposal will be made in December after it hears from bureaucrats on each issue.
